Since V^n is finite-dimensional, V^n ⊗_K Ω is finite-dimensional, and a finite-dimensional vector space spanned by eigenvectors has a basis consisting of eigenvectors. Thus F is diagonalizable on V^n ⊗_K Ω. By the characterization recalled at the beginning, F is semisimple on V^n. This holds for every integer n ≥ 0. The case r=0 is included: then V=K·1 and the same argument with the empty list of generators applies.

statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(\ell\neq p\) be a prime, and put \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\). Fix a nonzero element of \(\mathbb Q_\ell(1)\) and use it to identify Tate twists with \(\mathbb Q_\ell\). Let \(X\) be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension \(d\ge1\) over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(\xi\in H^2_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) be the cycle class of a divisor on \(X\) defined over \(\mathbb F_q\), and for each \(n\ge0\) let \(L:H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\to H^{n+2}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) be cup product with \(\xi\). Suppose that the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius \((\operatorname{id}\times\operatorname{Spec}\sigma)^*\), \(\sigma(c)=c^q\), is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every \(n\ge0\). Then \(F\) is semisimple on \(\ker L\subseteq H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every \(n\ge0\).
proof:
Let V^n = H^n_et(X_k,Q_ℓ). By lemma_45_finite_frob applied to the constant sheaf Q_ℓ with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure (X is proper over F_q), each V^n is finite-dimensional over Q_ℓ. By lemma_6a, F = (id_{X_k}×Spec σ)^* is a Q_ℓ-linear automorphism of V^n, with inverse the geometric Frobenius.

Because ξ is the cycle class of a divisor D on X defined over F_q, lemma_291 with j=1 and m=1 gives F(ξ)=q ξ (under the fixed identification Q_ℓ(1)≅Q_ℓ).

By lemma_220, F is an automorphism of the graded Q_ℓ-algebra H^*_et(X_k,Q_ℓ) and satisfies F(a∪b)=F(a)∪F(b). Hence for every x∈V^n,
F(Lx)=F(ξ∪x)=F(ξ)∪F(x)=q ξ∪F(x)=q L(F(x)).
Since q∈Q_ℓ^×, this is equivalent to L(F(x))=q^{-1}F(Lx).

Now let x∈ker L. Then Lx=0, so L(Fx)=q^{-1}F(Lx)=0. Thus F(ker L)⊆ker L; i.e. W^n:=ker L is F-stable.

By hypothesis F is semisimple on V^n. Applying lemma_515 with K=Q_ℓ, V=V^n, T=F, and W=W^n gives that F|_{W^n} is semisimple. This holds for every n≥0. Therefore F is semisimple on ker L⊆H^n_et(X_k,Q_ℓ) for every n≥0. The argument is uniform for all n≥0, including n=0 and n>2d where the relevant spaces may be zero.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ℓ≠p be a prime, and put k equal to the algebraic closure of F_q. Let X and Y be smooth projective geometrically connected varieties of the same pure dimension d≥1 over F_q, and let f:Y→X be a proper surjective generically finite morphism of degree N≥1 over F_q. Let F_X and F_Y be the q-power arithmetic Frobenius automorphisms (id×Spec σ)^*, σ(c)=c^q, acting on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ℓ) and H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ℓ) for every n≥0. Suppose F_Y is semisimple on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_ℓ) for every n≥0. Then F_X is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ℓ) for every n≥0.
proof:
Notation. Let k be the algebraic closure of F_q and let σ: k → k, σ(c) = c^q. For an F_q-scheme Z put Z_k = Z ×_{F_q} Spec k and Φ_Z := id_{Z_k} ×_{Spec k} Spec σ: Z_k → Z_k (under the identification Z_k = Z ×_{F_q} Spec k this is the same as id_Z ×_{F_q} Spec σ). Then F_Z := Φ_Z^* is the q-power arithmetic Frobenius on H^*_et(Z_k, Q_ℓ). Thus F_X = Φ_X^* and F_Y = Φ_Y^*, exactly as in the statement.

Step 1 (finite-dimensionality and invertibility). X and Y are projective over F_q, hence proper. Apply lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_45_finite_frob with K = Q_ℓ the constant sheaf on X_k (resp. on Y_k) equipped with its natural arithmetic Frobenius structure: it gives that V := H^n_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) and W := H^n_et(Y_k, Q_ℓ) are finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector spaces for every n ≥ 0. By lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a, F_X is a Q_ℓ-linear automorphism of V and F_Y is a Q_ℓ-linear automorphism of W; in particular F_X ∈ GL(V) and F_Y ∈ GL(W).

Step 2 (Frobenius equivariance of pullback). Let f_k := f ×_{F_q} id_{Spec k}: Y_k → X_k. The morphisms f_k, Φ_X, Φ_Y are all morphisms of F_q-schemes, and composition in fibre products over Spec F_q is componentwise, so
Φ_X ∘ f_k = (id_X × σ) ∘ (f × id_{Spec k}) = (id_X ∘ f) × (σ ∘ id_{Spec k}) = f × σ,
f_k ∘ Φ_Y = (f × id_{Spec k}) ∘ (id_Y × σ) = (f ∘ id_Y) × (id_{Spec k} ∘ σ) = f × σ.
Hence Φ_X ∘ f_k = f_k ∘ Φ_Y as morphisms Y_k → X_k. Applying the contravariant functor H^n_et(−, Q_ℓ) and using functoriality of pullback ((g ∘ h)^* = h^* ∘ g^*), we obtain
(★)  f_k^* ∘ F_X = F_Y ∘ f_k^*  on H^n_et(X_k, Q_ℓ).
Write f^* := f_k^*.

Step 3 (injectivity). Since f is in particular a surjective morphism of smooth projective geometrically connected varieties over F_q and ℓ ≠ p, lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_375 gives that f^*: V → W is injective for every n ≥ 0.

Step 4 (a Frobenius-stable copy of V inside W). Fix n ≥ 0 and set W' := f^*(V) ⊆ W. By (★), for every v ∈ V we have F_Y(f^*v) = f^*(F_X v) ∈ W'; hence F_Y(W') ⊆ W'. The restriction of F_Y to W' is injective (F_Y is injective on W by Step 1), so dim F_Y(W') = dim W'; combined with F_Y(W') ⊆ W' this gives F_Y(W') = W'. Therefore F_Y|_{W'} is a Q_ℓ-linear automorphism of W'.

Step 5 (restriction to a stable subspace). By hypothesis F_Y is semisimple on W; W is finite-dimensional and F_Y ∈ GL(W) by Step 1. Lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_358, applied to T = F_Y and to the F_Y-stable subspace W' ⊆ W, yields that F_Y|_{W'} is semisimple on W'.

Step 6 (transport back to V). By Step 3 the map f^*: V → W' is a Q_ℓ-linear isomorphism (injective by Step 3, surjective onto W' by the definition of W'), and by (★) it satisfies f^* ∘ F_X = (F_Y|_{W'}) ∘ f^*. Both F_X ∈ GL(V) and F_Y|_{W'} ∈ GL(W') are invertible (Step 1 and Step 4). Lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_8, applied to α = f^*, T_V = F_X and T_W = F_Y|_{W'}, therefore gives: F_X is semisimple on V if and only if F_Y|_{W'} is semisimple on W'. By Step 5 the latter holds, so F_X is semisimple on V = H^n_et(X_k, Q_ℓ).

Step 7. Since n ≥ 0 was arbitrary, F_X is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k, Q_ℓ) for every n ≥ 0, which is the assertion.

Remark (geometric Frobenius). By lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_6a the geometric Frobenius on V is F_X^{-1}. Since V is finite-dimensional, Cayley–Hamilton gives F_X^{-1} ∈ Q_ℓ[F_X], and conversely F_X ∈ Q_ℓ[F_X^{-1}]; hence the Q_ℓ[F_X]-submodules and the Q_ℓ[F_X^{-1}]-submodules of V coincide, so F_X is semisimple on V if and only if F_X^{-1} is. Thus the conclusion holds equally for geometric Frobenius, in the form stated in the conjecture.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ℓ≠p be a prime, let m≥1 be an integer, and put k = algebraic closure of F_q. Let A be an abelian surface over F_{q^m}. Fix a nonzero element of ℚ_ℓ(1) and use it to identify Tate twists with ℚ_ℓ. Let ξ∈H²_ét(A_k,ℚ_ℓ) be the cycle class of an F_{q^m}-rational very ample divisor on A, and let L be cup product with ξ. Then the ℚ_ℓ-linear map L: H¹_ét(A_k,ℚ_ℓ)→H³_ét(A_k,ℚ_ℓ) is an isomorphism.
proof:
Put Q=q^m and V=H^1_et(A_k,Q_l). Since A is an abelian surface, it is smooth projective and geometrically connected of pure dimension 2 over F_Q. Fix the given identification Q_l(1)=Q_l; all Tate twists are identified with Q_l.

First establish the exterior-algebra structure. By [Spark/043be352939fa7b2/lemma_cohom_abelian_variety_hopf_algebra], H^*=⊕_{n≥0} H^n_et(A_k,Q_l), with cup product and the Hopf-algebra structure coming from the group law of A, is a graded-commutative, graded-cocommutative Hopf algebra over Q_l with H^0=Q_l. By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_499_h1_dimension_abelian_variety] applied to the abelian surface A over F_Q, dim V=2·2=4. By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_projective_cohomology_vanishes_above_twice_dimension], H^n=0 for n>4. By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_77] with d=2, the trace map tr_A:H^4→Q_l(-2)≅Q_l is an isomorphism, so dim H^4=1, and for every n the pairing H^n×H^{4-n}→Q_l, (x,y)↦tr_A(x∪y), is perfect. Thus H^3 is dual to V and H^4 is finite-dimensional. For H^2, the perfect pairing H^2×H^2→Q_l gives H^2≅(H^2)^*; an infinite-dimensional vector space is not isomorphic to its dual (if dim H^2=κ were infinite, then dim (H^2)^*=|Q_l|^κ≥2^κ>κ), so H^2 is finite-dimensional. Hence H^* is finite-dimensional. Applying [eoinm/c9a724f5aa70a2d3/eca874] with N=4 (we have dim H^1=4, H^n=0 for n>4, and dim H^4=1) gives, for every n≥0, an isomorphism Λ^n V→H^n induced by cup product. In particular H^2=Λ^2 V, H^3=Λ^3 V, H^4=Λ^4 V, and cup product corresponds to wedge product.

Now let ξ∈H^2=Λ^2 V be the given class. Define β_ξ:V×V→Q_l by β_ξ(x,y)=tr_A(x∪y∪ξ). Since x,y have degree 1, β_ξ(y,x)=-β_ξ(x,y), so β_ξ is alternating. Choose an ordered basis e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4 of V and put τ=tr_A(e_1∧e_2∧e_3∧e_4)∈Q_l^×; this is nonzero because tr_A is an isomorphism and e_1∧e_2∧e_3∧e_4 is a nonzero basis vector of Λ^4 V=H^4. Write ξ=∑_{1≤i<j≤4} a_{ij} e_i∧e_j with a_{ij}∈Q_l. A direct computation in the exterior algebra gives β_ξ(e_1,e_2)=τ a_{34}, β_ξ(e_1,e_3)=-τ a_{24}, β_ξ(e_1,e_4)=τ a_{23}, β_ξ(e_2,e_3)=τ a_{14}, β_ξ(e_2,e_4)=-τ a_{13}, β_ξ(e_3,e_4)=τ a_{12}. Hence the Pfaffian of the alternating matrix M=(β_ξ(e_i,e_j)) is Pf(M)=τ^2(a_{12}a_{34}-a_{13}a_{24}+a_{14}a_{23}). On the other hand, ξ∧ξ=2(a_{12}a_{34}-a_{13}a_{24}+a_{14}a_{23}) e_1∧e_2∧e_3∧e_4. We claim that ξ^2≠0. Let H be the F_Q-rational very ample divisor whose cycle class, after the fixed identification Q_l(1)=Q_l, is ξ. It is ample. By [eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_272] applied over F_Q, deg(cl(H)^2) is the image in Q_l of a positive rational number. Under the fixed Tate identification, tr_A(ξ^2)=deg(cl(H)^2), because both maps send the class of a closed point z to [κ(z):F_Q]. Thus tr_A(ξ^2)≠0, so ξ^2≠0. Therefore the coefficient in ξ∧ξ is nonzero, and hence Pf(M)≠0. For an alternating 4×4 matrix, det M=Pf(M)^2, so det M≠0. Thus β_ξ is nondegenerate.

Finally, the map L:V→H^3 is Q_l-linear because cup product is bilinear. For y∈V, L(y)=y∪ξ. If L(y)=0, then for every x∈V, β_ξ(x,y)=tr_A(x∪y∪ξ)=tr_A(x∪L(y))=0. Since β_ξ is nondegenerate, y=0. Hence L is injective. By the exterior-algebra isomorphism, dim H^3=dim Λ^3 V=4 choose 3=4=dim V. Therefore L is an isomorphism.

statement: Let \(q=p^a\) be a prime power, let \(\ell\neq p\) be a prime, and put \(k=\overline{\mathbb F}_q\). Let \(X\) be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension \(d\ge1\) over \(\mathbb F_q\), let \(Z\subset X\) be a smooth closed subvariety of pure codimension \(c\) with \(1\le c\le d\), defined over \(\mathbb F_q\), and let \(\pi:\widetilde X=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X\to X\) be the blow-up of \(X\) along \(Z\). Then the \(q\)-power arithmetic Frobenius is semisimple on \(H^n_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(\widetilde X_k,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for every integer \(n\ge0\).

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ℓ≠p be a prime, and put k equal to the algebraic closure of F_q. Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of pure dimension d≥0 over F_q. Suppose there exists a filtration ∅=X_{-1}⊂X_0⊂…⊂X_d=X by closed subschemes defined over F_q such that for every i with 0≤i≤d, the open subscheme X_i∖X_{i-1} is isomorphic over F_q to a disjoint union of finitely many copies of A^i_{F_q}. Then the q-power arithmetic Frobenius (id×Spec σ)^*, σ(c)=c^q, is semisimple on H^n_et(X_k,Q_ℓ) for every n≥0.
proof:
We prove a stronger assertion P(s). For s≥0, let Y be a proper F_q-scheme of finite type equipped with a filtration ∅=Y_{-1}⊂Y_0⊂...⊂Y_s=Y by closed F_q-subschemes such that for each i=0,...,s the stratum U_i=Y_i\Y_{i-1} is isomorphic over F_q to a finite disjoint union of copies of A^i_{F_q} (zero copies allowed). Then: (1) H^n_et(Y_k,Q_l)=0 for every n>2s; and (2) the q-power arithmetic Frobenius F=(id×Spec σ)^*, σ(c)=c^q, acts semisimply on H^n_et(Y_k,Q_l) for every n≥0.

Base case s=0. Here Y=U_0 is isomorphic over F_q to a finite disjoint union of copies of A^0_{F_q}=Spec F_q. After base change, Y_k is a finite disjoint union of copies of Spec k. Since k is separably closed, H^0_et(Spec k,Q_l)=Q_l and H^n_et(Spec k,Q_l)=0 for n>0. By additivity over disjoint unions (lemma_cohom_open_closed_sum), H^0_et(Y_k,Q_l) is a finite direct sum of copies of Q_l and H^n_et(Y_k,Q_l)=0 for n>0. On each copy of Spec k the Frobenius acts as the identity on H^0, so F is diagonalizable with eigenvalue 1 on H^0 and the higher cohomology vanishes. Thus P(0) holds.

Induction step. Assume P(s-1) for some s≥1. Let Y=Y_s, Z=Y_{s-1}, and U=Y\Z. Since Z is a closed subscheme of the proper scheme Y, it is proper, and it inherits the filtration of length s-1, so P(s-1) applies to Z. Put W^n=H^n_et(Z_k,Q_l), V^n=H^n_et(Y_k,Q_l), and C^n=H^n_{c,et}(U_k,Q_l). By induction, W^n=0 for n>2s-2, and F is semisimple on every W^n.

By hypothesis U is isomorphic over F_q to a finite disjoint union of N copies of A^s_{F_q}, with N≥0. Additivity over disjoint unions (lemma_cohom_open_closed_sum) together with the standard compact-support cohomology of affine space (lemma_hc_affine_space) gives C^n=0 for n≠2s and C^{2s}≅Q_l^N. By lemma_286, the q-power arithmetic Frobenius acts on H^{2s}_{c,et}(A^s_k,Q_l) as multiplication by q^s. Hence F acts on C^{2s} as the scalar q^s; if N=0 then C^{2s}=0 and the assertion is vacuous.

The localization exact sequence for the closed immersion Z⊂Y with open complement U (lemma_localization_les_finite_type) is a long exact sequence of Q_l[F]-modules
... → C^n → H^n_{c,et}(Y_k,Q_l) → H^n_{c,et}(Z_k,Q_l) → C^{n+1} → ... .
Because Y and Z are proper, compactly supported cohomology coincides with ordinary cohomology for them: for a proper morphism f one has Rf_!=Rf_*. Therefore the sequence becomes
... → C^n → V^n → W^n → C^{n+1} → ... .

We now analyze the possible n.

Case 1: n is not 2s-1 and not 2s. Then C^n=C^{n+1}=0, so the sequence gives 0→V^n→W^n→0. Thus V^n≅W^n as F-modules, and F is semisimple on V^n by the induction hypothesis. If n>2s, then n>2s-2, so W^n=0 by induction, and hence V^n=0.

Case 2: n=2s-1. Since C^{2s-1}=0, the sequence gives an injection 0→V^{2s-1}→W^{2s-1}. Thus V^{2s-1} is an F-stable subspace of W^{2s-1}. A restriction of a semisimple operator to an invariant subspace is semisimple: the minimal polynomial of the restriction divides the squarefree minimal polynomial of F on W^{2s-1}. Hence F is semisimple on V^{2s-1}.

Case 3: n=2s. By induction W^{2s}=0, because 2s>2s-2, and also C^{2s+1}=0. The exact sequence gives C^{2s}→V^{2s}→W^{2s}=0, so C^{2s}→V^{2s} is surjective. Therefore V^{2s} is a quotient of C^{2s}. Since F acts on C^{2s} as the scalar q^s, it acts on the quotient V^{2s} as the same scalar q^s (or V^{2s}=0 when C^{2s}=0). In particular F is semisimple on V^{2s}.

Case 4: n>2s. This is included in Case 1, since n is neither 2s-1 nor 2s; hence V^n≅W^n=0.

All n≥0 are covered. Thus P(s) holds.

Finally, the given X is a proper F_q-scheme of finite type, and its filtration ∅=X_{-1}⊂X_0⊂...⊂X_d=X has strata X_i\X_{i-1} isomorphic over F_q to finite disjoint unions of copies of A^i_{F_q}. Applying P(d) with Y=X gives that the q-power arithmetic Frobenius acts semisimply on H^n_et(X_k,Q_l) for every n≥0. This is exactly the required statement.

statement: Let q=p^a be a prime power, let ℓ≠p be a prime, let V be a finite-dimensional Q_ℓ-vector space, let F be an automorphism of V, and let N be a nilpotent endomorphism of V with N F = q F N. Suppose V has a finite F-stable filtration W_• by Q_ℓ-subspaces such that N(W_i)⊆W_{i-2} for every i and each graded piece gr_i^W is pure of weight i, meaning every eigenvalue α of F on gr_i^W satisfies |ι(α)|=q^{i/2} for every embedding ι of the algebraic closure of Q_ℓ into C. If F is semisimple on gr_i^W for every i, then F is semisimple on V.
proof:
Proof. Put K := Q_ℓ and let K̄ be an algebraic closure of K. For an operator T on a finite-dimensional K-vector space we say that T is semisimple if the K[t]-module structure on the space given by t·x := T(x) is semisimple; this is the sense in which the word is used in the cited lemma. In fact we prove the conclusion from the following weaker hypotheses, which are the only ones used: W_• is a finite F-stable filtration by K-subspaces, each graded piece gr_i^W is pure of weight i, and F is semisimple on every gr_i^W. The nilpotent endomorphism N and the relations N F = q F N and N(W_i) ⊆ W_{i−2} are never used below; in particular no claim that W_• is the monodromy filtration of N is made or needed.

Conventions on W_•. A finite filtration indexed by Z means that all but finitely many of the W_i coincide, with W_i = 0 for all i sufficiently negative and W_i = V for all i sufficiently positive; explicitly, there are integers c ≤ d with W_i = 0 for all i < c and W_i = V for all i > d. (If the filtration is instead presented as a finite increasing sequence 0 = W_{a−1} ⊆ W_a ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ W_b = V, take those integers a ≤ b and go directly to Step 2; Steps 0–1 then merely record that this case is covered.) Let D := {i ∈ Z : W_i ≠ W_{i−1}}; this is a finite set.

Step 0 (trivial case). If V = 0 then every operator on V is semisimple (the zero space is the empty direct sum of simple modules), so assume V ≠ 0; then D ≠ ∅.

Step 1 (trimming the filtration). Let a := min D and b := max D. I claim that W_{a−1} = 0 and W_b = V. Indeed, for every i ≤ a−1 we have i ∉ D, hence W_i = W_{i−1}; so W_i = W_{a−1} for all i ≤ a−1, and taking i < min(c, a) gives W_{a−1} = W_i = 0. Likewise, for every i ≥ b+1 we have i ∉ D, hence W_i = W_{i−1}; so W_i = W_b for all i ≥ b, and taking i > max(d, b) gives W_b = W_i = V. Thus 0 = W_{a−1} ⊆ W_a ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ W_b = V is an increasing, exhaustive, separated filtration of V by F-stable K-subspaces (F-stability is inherited from W_•). Moreover gr_i^W = W_i/W_{i−1} = 0 for every i ∉ [a, b], and for i ∈ [a, b] the space gr_i^W is exactly the graded piece to which the purity hypothesis refers, hence is pure of weight i.

Step 2 (the induced operators). For every i we have F(W_i) ⊆ W_i and F(W_{i−1}) ⊆ W_{i−1}, so F induces a K-linear map F_i : gr_i^W → gr_i^W, x + W_{i−1} ↦ F(x) + W_{i−1}. Since dim_K W_i < ∞ and F is injective, dim_K F(W_i) = dim_K W_i; as F(W_i) ⊆ W_i, this gives F(W_i) = W_i. Hence F_i is surjective, and being an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space it is bijective, i.e. F_i ∈ GL_K(gr_i^W). Let χ_i(t) := det(t·id − F_i) ∈ K[t] be its characteristic polynomial; by convention χ_i = 1 when gr_i^W = 0.

Step 3 (pairwise coprimeness of the χ_i). Let i ≠ j be elements of [a, b], and let α ∈ K̄ be a common root of χ_i and χ_j. Over the algebraically closed field K̄ the roots of the characteristic polynomial of a linear operator are exactly its eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity; hence α is an eigenvalue of F_i and of F_j, i.e. an eigenvalue of F on gr_i^W and on gr_j^W. Fix one embedding ι : K̄ → C (K has characteristic 0, so such embeddings exist, and the purity hypothesis is stated for every embedding, hence for this one). By purity of gr_i^W (weight i) and gr_j^W (weight j) we get |ι(α)| = q^{i/2} and |ι(α)| = q^{j/2}. Therefore q^{i/2} = q^{j/2}; squaring yields q^i = q^j, and since q = p^a ≥ 2 > 1 we conclude i = j, contradicting i ≠ j. Hence χ_i and χ_j have no common root in K̄. Since K[t] is a principal ideal domain and K̄ is an algebraic closure of K, two polynomials of K[t] have a common root in K̄ if and only if their gcd in K[t] is nonconstant (a nonconstant gcd has a root in K̄, which is then a common root; conversely a common root α gives the common factor t − α). Therefore gcd(χ_i, χ_j) = 1 in K[t] for all distinct i, j ∈ [a, b]. (If gr_i^W = 0 then χ_i = 1 and the assertion is immediate; the argument above also covers this case, since χ_i then has no root.)

Step 4 (semisimplicity on the graded pieces). By hypothesis, F is semisimple on gr_i^W for every integer i; in particular, for every i ∈ [a, b], the operator F_i induced by F on gr_i^W is semisimple. (No condition is needed for i ∉ [a, b], where gr_i^W = 0.)

Step 5 (applying the filtered criterion). Apply lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_531 to K = Q_ℓ (a field of characteristic 0), the finite-dimensional K-vector space V, the automorphism F ∈ GL_K(V), the integers a ≤ b, and the increasing exhaustive separated filtration 0 = W_{a−1} ⊆ W_a ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ W_b = V by F-stable K-subspaces. Its two hypotheses are exactly Steps 3 and 4: the characteristic polynomials in K[t] of the operators induced by F on gr_i^W and on gr_j^W are coprime for all distinct i, j ∈ [a, b], and F is semisimple on gr_i^W for every i ∈ [a, b]. The lemma therefore yields that F is semisimple on V, which is the assertion. ∎
